title: Injective acyclicity gives sheaf-level base change for arbitrary coefficients
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Assume coefficient-wise injective acyclicity: for every prime $\ell$, every morphism $g:Y'\to Y$, every cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with induced $f':X'\to Y'$ and $g':X'\to X$, and every injective sheaf $I$ of $(\Lambda/\ell)_X$-modules on $X_{\Et}$, one has $R^qf'_*g'^{-1}I=0$ for all $q>0$ (higher direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] of the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] of the underlying abelian sheaf). Then for every such square and every sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda_X$-modules with torsion underlying abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$, regarded as a complex concentrated in degree 0, the derived exchange morphism $\Ex_{\square,F}:g^{-1}Rf_*F\to Rf'_*g'^{-1}F$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] is an isomorphism in $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories].

proof.text: For every prime l and every cartesian square, apply the canonical inverse-image coefficient comparison [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-inverse-image-comparison] and the canonical derived direct-image coefficient comparison [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-derived-direct-image-comparison] to the degree-zero complex of g'^{-1}I. Exact forgetting commutes with homology, so the hypothesis identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of its positive module-valued higher direct image with a zero object. Faithfulness of forgetting reflects the equation id = 0. Thus f has module-valued HasInjectiveAcyclicity over Lambda/l for every prime l.

Apply the existing coefficient-wise theorem hasTorsionBaseChange_of_hasInjectiveAcyclicity of [lemma-weil-pbc-property-iff-acyclicity] in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Etale.BaseChangeTheorems.Coefficients. Its proof first uses the injective-resolution/underived-exchange argument for the torsion rings Lambda/l, and then prime-factor devissage and filtered-colimit passage. This reuses, without bypassing, the unit sk-thm-iff route and yields the module-valued exchange isomorphism on every bounded-below complex with torsion homology.

By [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations], the filtration definition of torsion assumed for the underlying abelian sheaf of F is equivalent to local torsion. The existing isTorsionModuleSheaf_iff_isTorsion identifies this with torsion of the module sheaf F. The degree-zero complex of F has torsion homology: degree zero is F, and every other homology sheaf is zero. Apply Step 2 to this complex.

The fixed compatibility equation of [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-derived-exchange-compatibility] identifies the forgotten module exchange followed by its invertible target comparison with its invertible source comparison followed by abelian exchange. Functors preserve isomorphisms, so cancellation proves invertibility of the specified abelian exchange on the forgotten module complex. The natural isomorphism commuting exact forgetting with the degree-zero embedding, and naturality of derived exchange, transport this to exactly the complex in the conclusion.
